prompt: Stage 2-6, level 5, 85 HP after two losses. Your tank stands on the far left of the front row and your bruiser on the far right; carry and caster are in the back. Both fights went the same way: the enemy melee walked straight down the middle, your two frontliners each fought one enemy on the edge, and the carry died. What is the fix?

options.label: Move the tank and the bruiser to the centre of the front row, side by side, so every enemy walking up the middle bumps into them first
Keep them on the corners: two separate fronts split the enemy's attention and each frontliner only fights one enemy
Move the carry to the front row between the two frontliners so it is protected on both sides

explanation:
Enemies walk toward the nearest unit. With your front line on the two far corners, the nearest unit for anyone walking up the middle is your support and then your carries; the tank and bruiser are on the edges catching one enemy each and standing next to nothing. A front line only works when it is a line: the two bodies side by side in the centre, (0,2) and (0,3) or (0,3) and (0,4), so the whole enemy team runs into them and the fight happens there, four hexes from the carry.

'Two fronts split the enemy's attention' sounds clever and is the exact reason you lost twice: the enemy did not split, it walked between them. Moving the carry into the front line is worse still: a carry in row 0 is the first thing hit, and it is the one unit on the board that cannot take it. Keep the front together, keep the carry behind it.
principle: A frontline is a line: tanks side by side in the centre so the enemy runs into them, not between them.
commonMistake: Spreading the tanks to the two corners 'to cover both sides', which leaves the middle open and the carry as the closest target.
hint: Trace the path the enemy melee took both times. Which of your units was the closest thing on that path?
